national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India has taken fintech journey to new heights, with innovation and inclusion at its core. He said, technologies like Agentic AI, tokenisation and quantum are opening new possibilities in the financial sector. Mr. Modi said this while addressing the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai this evening. The Prime Minister hailed UPI as a champion of fintech, noting that more than two thousand four hundred crore UPI transactions were recorded in last month. He said Indian UPI is now operational in eleven countries. Mr. Modi stressed that global collaboration in fintech systems should be new goal to reduce transaction costs in remittances. Prime Minister urged stakeholders at the GFF 2026 to use Fintech as a tool for financial inclusion. The Prime Minister also called upon fintech firms to build top notch cyber security, ethical data production standards, strong Fintech regulated industry innovation ecosystem and Fintech Protection Consumer Index. Lauding the country’s remarkable GDP growth in the last quarter, Mr. Modi said, world has gained reassurance from India’s 7.8 percent growth despite challenging global conflicts, uncertainties and stress on global supply chains of energy and commodities. He also highlighted that the Japan Credit Rating Agency has upgraded country’s sovereign credit rating from BBB+ to A- with a stable outlook, returning India to the A rating category after more than three decades. The four-day Global Fintech Fest 2026 is being held in Mumbai from 8th to 11th September. The theme of this year’s fest is Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum – Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 96 Russia backs India’s peace efforts to end Ukraine conflict
national_raw_news.content: Russia today said it would welcome any peace efforts by India to end the Ukraine conflict, noting that Moscow’s strategy aligns closely with New Delhi’s position for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy. Addressing media at a virtual briefing in New Delhi this afternoon ahead of the BRICS Summit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said they know the position of India on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent, it corresponds with their own position because they do want the solution to the Ukraine conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open for this process. Mr. Peskov said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold bilateral talks on the sidelines of BRICS Summit. He said, both leaders are expected to discuss issues of mutual interest. Mr Peskov added that that it will also be an opportunity for President Putin to inform Prime Minister Modi about the situation on the war with Ukraine. He said both leaders are in close personal contact and very pragmatic in their relationship. He said both leaders are able to discuss sensitive matters in open and constructive ways. Replying to a question on trade imbalance netween India and Russia, the Kremlin spokesman said Indian side has raised the issue of trade deficit with Russian side. He further stated that in order to address this imbalance, Russian businesses and companies are now looking for additional goods that can be purchased from India and joint projects that could be launched in India. On import of Russian energy by India, Mr Peskov stated that a new record is set every month but refused to give exact figures. He called sanctions against countries trading with Russia as unacceptable and illegal. He emphasised that it is illegal to attempt to introduce limitations on international trade and to threaten other countries and third parties for doing trade with others. Replying to another query, Mr Peskov maintained that BRICS is against no one. He said BRICS is for participating countries, and for their national interests. He said cooperation in BRICS is based on mutual trust, mutual respect, mutual benefits and trade. He added that these ideals are shared by all the member states. The Kremlin spokesman said that AI would be high on the agenda during the BRICS Summit. He said Russia considers India to be very important partner in the global majority.
